name: Tarrenz
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Gurgltal valley, home to Burg Altstarkenberg and the annual Tarrenzer Fest – steeped in tradition.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Tarrenz is situated at an elevation of 836 meters in the Tyrolean Gurgltal, a sun-blessed valley between the regional capital of Imst and the Fern Pass. Home to approximately 2,830 residents in the district of Imst, this storied municipality spreads out beneath the imposing massif of the Tschirgant and the Lechtal Alps. Renowned as the mythical Witches' Village (Hexendorf) with ancestral carnival traditions, Tarrenz looks back upon a rich medieval mining heritage. Furthermore, the village is the proud home of the historic castle brewery Schloss Starkenberg, famous worldwide for its beer swimming pools. Its scenic valley floor, historic estates, and lush alpine meadows offer a versatile haven for cultural travelers, outdoor families, and hikers.

Geschichte

Settlement in the Gurgltal dates back to the Bronze and Roman eras, when the historic Via Claudia Augusta crossed the nearby Fern Pass. Tarrenz was first officially mentioned in 1265 as Torrens, deriving from the Latin word for a roaring mountain torrent. The High Middle Ages were deeply shaped by the powerful Lords of Starkenberg, who erected Altstarkenberg Castle in the 12th century and Neustarkenberg (now Schloss Starkenberg) around 1310 to control transit commerce over the pass. Following the Starkenberg Feud against Duke Frederick IV in the 1420s, the estate fell under the direct rule of the Tyrolean sovereigns. During the 15th and 16th centuries, the valley flourished as a vital lead and zinc mining center, providing essential metals for the silver smelters of Schwaz. Tarrenz's reputation as the Witches' Village is manifested in the quadrennial carnival pageant, where masked witches wearing hand-carved stone-pine masks with moveable jaws (Gschnapp) parade through the streets. The hilltop parish church of Saint Ulrich, consecrated in 1503, features a monumental fresco of Saint Christopher dating to roughly 1520.

Anreise

Tarrenz enjoys direct and straightforward transport links from both the Inntal and Bavaria. Drivers from Germany can travel completely toll-free via Füssen, Reutte, and the B179 Fernpassstraße, continuing along the B189 directly to Tarrenz. From Innsbruck or Vorarlberg, motorists take the Inntalautobahn A12 to the Imst/Pitztal exit, reaching the village in just four kilometers. Rail travelers arrive at the Imst-Pitztal railway station on the Arlberg line, served by frequent ÖBB Railjets and regional trains. From the station and the Imst central bus terminal, VVT regional buses provide frequent connections reaching Tarrenz in approximately ten minutes.

Tipps

Schloss Starkenberg offers a truly memorable excursion: visitors can tour the historic Biermythos brewery cellars and even soak in the world's first beer swimming pools, bathing in warm water infused with mineral-rich brewer's yeast. Directly adjacent, the open-air museum Knappenwelt Gurgltal reconstructs a 16th-century Tyrolean mining settlement across nine authentic timber buildings, featuring an exhibition on the archaeological discovery of the 17th-century Healer of Gurgltal. Outdoor enthusiasts should not miss the breathtaking Salvesenschlucht gorge, where a secure circular hiking trail crosses the Hoher Übergang – an airy suspension bridge forty meters above the roaring canyon – alongside charming wooden sculpture trails and the mythical Witches' Oven.
